text:
Maria (Sales): Hey team, Polaris Logistics wants a short POC benchmark for a mixed workload next week. They want: 1) embeddings lookup + chat inference in same flow, 2) sustained 150 QPS with 1s latency p50 target for chat, occasional 400–500 QPS bursts, 3) cost estimate for hosted vs. dedicated, and 4) confirmation on KMS/HSM + audit logs for SOC2. Attach their security questionnaire here: https://polaris.s3/procurement/sec-qa.pdf :wave:

Ajay (Eng): Thanks — do we know model families? small-chat + embed-1 OK? Also need typical token sizes.

Maria (Sales): They said chat ~80 tokens avg, embeddings requests are batched in groups of 16 (each ~512 tokens). Models: chat-small-v1 and embed-s-512.

Sam (SRE): For sustaining 150 QPS chat at ~80 tokens we should be fine on 4x A10s in a dedicated pool with batching. Bursts to 500QPS => recommend burst pool or autoscale window. Will note tail latency risk.

Nina (Solutions): For hosted pricing quick calc: rough cost = tokens * unit rate + concurrency premium. I'll sketch numbers, but sales wants a single-slide estimate.

Ajay (Eng): Quick smoke script we can run for mixed flow (k6 + curl):
```
// k6 pseudo
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  // embeddings batch of 16
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', JSON.stringify({model:'embed-s-512', inputs:['...']*16}));
  // then chat call
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', JSON.stringify({model:'chat-small-v1', prompt:'...'}));
}
```
Use `--vus` to shape burst and `--duration` for sustain.

Maria (Sales): Can someone run an initial hosted run tomorrow and post numbers? They need 150QPS verified and a cost delta vs dedicated. Also procurement flagged KMS + HSM latency overhead — they want that quantified.

Sam (SRE): I'll spin a hosted test. Quick notes: enabling CMK (customer-managed key) adds ~5–12ms per token on our current pipeline (measured on similar setups). I'll validate.

Ajay (Eng): If we run dedicated we can avoid HSM path on token hot path (KMS only for model keys + audit). That saves latency but has compliance tradeoffs. I'll prepare an A/B config: CMK-on-hosted vs Dedicated+KMS.

Nina (Solutions): For cost: sample calc below (very rough):
- Hosted: tokens (chat+embed) * $0.0009 + per-request overhead ~ 10% => est $0.12/request at 150QPS sustained
- Dedicated: amortized GPU + infra + support => est $0.06/request at same throughput (depends on commit)
I'll turn into slide numbers.

deploy-bot: triggered run: hosted-mixed-bench-3867000000 started by Sam (SRE) at 2026-03-21T09:12:05Z :rocket:

Sam (SRE): Initial hosted run (short): sustain 150QPS for 10m, 99th chat latency 210ms, p50 95ms, embeddings batch p50 60ms. CMK-on test increased chat p50 +8ms. CPU steady, GPU utilization ~72% on our instance shapes.

Maria (Sales): awesome — can you add a quick summary for the prospect and a one-line recommendation? I'll put on the slide for tomorrow's exec call.

Ajay (Eng): Recommendation: run initial POC on hosted to validate integration + security question answers. If Polaris needs consistent sustained throughput at low unit cost and strict KMS/HSM separation, move to Dedicated with burst pool and optional HSM for key operations (explain tradeoff: +compliance, +audit, ~+5–15ms overhead if HSM in the token path).

Nina (Solutions): Action items: 1) Sam to attach raw perf logs + quick grafana dashboard link, 2) Ajay to draft two config options and latency impact, 3) Nina to produce cost slide, 4) Maria to send security QA answers.

Maria (Sales): Thanks — will coordinate slide and procurement. If you can drop the logs & exact commands in thread I'll forward. :thumbsup:

Sam (SRE): Uploading logs now: https://internal.redwood/incoming/polaris/3867000000/logs.tar.gz

Ajay (Eng): Commands used (copyable):
`k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m mixedflow.js`
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/bench/start -d '{"config":"mixedflow", "target_qps":150}'`

Maria (Sales): perfect, thanks everyone — sending to Polaris procurement and looping in their security lead.

Nina (Solutions): I'll draft the slide and ping for review in ~2 hours.
